text:
name: summer_playlist_maker
does: Builds a playlist of upbeat songs for a party or a backyard barbecue.
inputs: the mood or event, and how long the playlist should be
people say:
- Something happy for the cookout, please
- Put on songs for the ball game party
- I'm going to grill tonight, get me some good music
- Make a mix about two hours long, nothing too slow
- Brown Sugar has to be in there, so build it around that

name: takeaway_order_helper
does: Places a takeaway order at a restaurant and says when it will be ready.
inputs: the restaurant, the dishes, and a pickup time
people say:
- I want food to go from the noodle place
- Get me one small coffee and a sandwich to take away
- Have my usual ready at six
- Please load my last order again, same as Friday
- Order two soups for pickup in half an hour

In autumn the weather gets cooler, and many people start to care about temperature numbers. A thermometer shows how warm or cold it is, and most places use either Celsius or Fahrenheit. If you grew up with one and then visit a place that uses the other, the numbers look strange. A weather app can change the scale for you. People ask things like switch the temperature to Fahrenheit, show me degrees Celsius, or how much is sixty degrees in Celsius. The app will reply with the new number, and the setting stays that way until you change it back. A closed window and a warm coat are easier to choose when the number makes sense to you.

A kettle is for heating water fast. Some homes have an old boiler tucked in a cupboard that heats water for the whole house, but a kettle only heats what you need for a cup of tea. Most kettles let you choose a temperature, because green tea likes cooler water and coffee likes it almost boiling. People change the setting by saying make it hotter, set it to eighty degrees, or keep it warm for ten minutes. A smart kettle may also let you ask to start it from the sofa. Add a spoon of honey if you like your tea sweet, and turn the kettle off when you are done.

They want a reminder to pack the kitchen.
Remind me to pack the kitchen
Kitchen boxes, remind me please
Can you nudge me to wrap the dishes this weekend?
Post a note in the family channel so everyone remembers the kitchen still needs packing
Remind me tomorrow to wrap the plates and to throw out the stale crackers
I keep forgetting, so would you shuffle the kitchen to the top of my moving list?
It is almost moving day and the cupboards are still full, so could you please remind me on Thursday evening to start packing them?

When you shop or travel, a price may be in a different money than the one you use. An exchange rate tells you how much of your money you get for one unit of theirs. Rates move a little every day. Say you see a scooter for nine hundred euros on a website and you pay in dollars. You need the rate to know the real price. People ask how much is that in dollars, what is the rate today, or show the prices in pounds. An app can reduce the confusion by showing both prices side by side. A fast look at the rate before you pay can save you from a surprise on your card bill.

name: room_air_booster
does: Turns up the purifier or fan in one room and says how long it will run.
inputs: the room, and how strong or how long
people say:
- The air in here is stuffy
- Run the purifier in the bedroom for an hour
- I'm going to tidy the garage, so clear the dust out of the air
- The kids have a piano lesson in the den, keep the air fresh in there
- Switch the new filter fan to high

Priya got home from the hospital at eight in the morning after a long night shift. Her feet hurt and her eyes were heavy. She dropped her bag by the door and said to the speaker, "Find me a funny movie for tonight and tell me when the cinema down the road opens on Saturday." The assistant understood that she wanted two things: a comedy to watch and the Saturday opening time of the nearby cinema. It named three comedies and said the cinema opens at ten. Priya said the second film sounded perfect, so the assistant saved it to her watch list. Then she made tea so strong she could almost taste the leaves, glanced at the heating meter in the hall, and fell asleep on the sofa before the kettle had cooled.

name: yarn_planner
does: Estimates how much yarn and time a knitting project needs.
inputs: the thing to make, its size, and your knitting speed
people say:
- How much wool do I need for a tall scarf?
- I'm making a hat for my niece, what should I buy?
- Will three balls be enough for a baby blanket?
- How long will a sweater take if I knit slowly?
- Plan something to suit my taste, soft and green

Booking a hotel room means choosing a place, the nights you will stay, and how many guests are coming. The hotel asks for a name for the booking, and you show it at check-in, usually in the afternoon. Some places near airports offer hourly rooms for a short rest, but most charge by the night. People change a booking by saying move it one night later, add a guest, or put it under my sister's name. If you would rather camp, a tent has no check-in at all, but the ground is a lot harder.

Omar was late for his sister's wedding, still holding the iron he had used on his shirt. He cleared a small cough and said to his phone, "Excuse me, would you please take a picture of the cake table and send it to my mum, because she is sick at home today and she will be so sad if she misses it?" The assistant understood that he wanted a photo of the cake table and that it should go to his mum. The room was not very light, so it turned on the flash, took the picture, and sent it to the contact named Mum. Then it told Omar the photo was sent. He smiled, put down the iron, and ran for the car.

Greta knelt in the flower bed with a garden fork stuck in the soil. Her hands were too muddy to touch anything, and she wanted to wash them before using her phone, but rain was coming. So she typed with one knuckle: "play the local nwes on the radio, im busy". The assistant understood that she wanted the radio on, tuned to the local news station. It tuned in, and the news began to play from the phone on the garden table. A voice talked about road works and a village fair. Greta dug a round hole for the new rose and listened. When the weather report came on, she was glad she had asked, because it said rain would start at noon. She finished fast and went in to wash.

Sam was already pulling on his coat when he spoke to the kitchen display. "Tell me how much water we used this week and turn the water heater down, I have to run!" The assistant understood two requests: report the weekly water use, and lower the heater's temperature. It said the house used about two thousand litres, which was good news because it was less than last week. Then it lowered the heater from sixty to fifty degrees and said it was done. Sam heard that the bill could drop by a few dollars a month, nodded, and left. The display also showed the use rise for a moment, since the dishwasher had just started.

When you order food for delivery, you pick a place, choose your dishes, and give an address. The app shows when the food should arrive, and you can follow the driver on a map. People change things by saying make the order bigger, leave off the onions, deliver it later, or add a tip for the driver. A sandwich shop might ask if you want it cut in half. Kids may sing when the doorbell rings, and everyone is glad when the food comes hot. If it is late, people say where is my order or how much longer.

They want the call link opened for a meeting tomorrow at ten.
Join my call tomorrow at ten
Open the ten o'clock meeting link
Put the team call on my screen when it starts tomorrow
Can you open tomorrow's call at ten so the young designers can join and draw on the shared board?
I need to be on that video meeting tomorrow morning, ten sharp
Get everything in order and open the link before the call tomorrow at ten
Would you please start the meeting tomorrow at ten and let me know once everyone is in?

Dana was buckling her belt after a long day when her phone buzzed. She was cooking, with a child on each leg, so she said, "Read me the new text from school, and then reply that I will pick up Mia at four-thirty." The assistant understood that she wanted the message read out loud and a short answer sent back. It read that the school's monthly newsletter was out and that Mia needed a hat for the trip. Then it sent her reply. Dana said, "Mark that one as read, and remind me in twenty-five minutes to find the hat." The assistant marked the text as read and set a reminder for twenty-five minutes later.

Person: I want to go for a bike ride tomorrow. Can you find me a route?
Assistant: Happy to help. How far would you like to ride?
Person: Not too far. Half of what I did last week.
Assistant: I don't have last week's ride in front of me. How many kilometres was it?
Person: Oh dear. About twenty, I think.
Assistant: Then I'll look for a ten kilometre route. Should it go by the lake?
Person: Yes please. Is the water frozen this week?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't tell if the lake is frozen. I can show you the route and the weather, though.
Person: That's fine. Can you share the route with my son?
Assistant: Done, I sent it to him. Take extra water.

Lena stirred the pasta with one hand and held a can of tomatoes with the other when the phone buzzed on the counter. It was her mother, who often calls at dinner time. Lena could not pick up, so she said, "Answer on speaker, and then play the voicemail from this morning." The assistant understood both parts. It answered the call on the speaker so Lena could talk while she cooked. When the call ended, it played the voicemail, which was only twenty seconds long. Her mother had said that she would visit on Sunday. Lena laughed, said she would look forward to it, and went back to the pasta.

They want a notification when it is time to start their workout.
Notify me when it is time to exercise
Workout reminder at six
I sat all day and my legs feel like wood, so I should move soon
Tell me at half past five that I'm meant to be at the front of the yoga class
I had too much melon at lunch and feel heavy, so get me up around five
Hey, ping me before the gym closes tonight
It would be great if you could notify me an hour before leg day so that I can eat something light first

Bread rises because yeast makes tiny bubbles in the dough. Bakers wait until the dough is twice as big, then put it in a hot oven. People change a recipe by asking for more time, a hotter oven, or a smaller loaf. They say things like let it rise for another half hour, bake it ten minutes longer, or set the oven to two hundred degrees. In a small flat with a cold kitchen, you may need to organize a warm spot for the dough, such as the downstairs bathroom or near a radiator. A timer helps, and an assistant can set one when you say wake me when the dough is ready.

Ravi had been in the city for only two days. His hotel heater was broken and the morning was freezing, so he dressed in two jackets and stood on the corner with his phone. He typed fast in lowercase: "get me a taxi to the midle of town please". The assistant understood that he wanted a ride to the city centre. It booked a taxi, said the pickup point was the bus stop across the street, and told him the car would come in six minutes. Ravi walked to the stop, found the white car, and was warm again before he reached the middle of the old town.

name: resume_task_list
does: Brings back a list of tasks you paused and shows what is still unfinished.
inputs: the list name, and optionally the day you stopped
people say:
- Where did I stop yesterday?
- Show me what is left on the shopping list, I still need a pear
- Bring back my chores list
- Let me carry on with the list inside my work folder
- Which things are not done yet?

Hana's daughter had a Spanish quiz, and the sun was going down while Hana peeled carrots. She said to the speaker, "Tomorrow at seven I want to wake her up in Spanish, so how do I say good morning, my love?" The assistant understood that she wanted a Spanish phrase and some practice with it. It said buenos días, mi amor, and then repeated it slowly twice so that Hana could hear how it should sound. It was patient when she got the first word wrong. Then it offered to set an alarm for tomorrow at seven, and Hana said yes.

Leo was eight, and he sat at the kitchen table while the smell of garlic filled the room. Grandma had just visited and he wanted her number saved. He typed on the tablet in a hurry: "add grandma to my contacts her numbr is 555 0142". The assistant understood that he wanted a new contact named Grandma with that phone number. It saved her and asked if it should also save her birthday. Leo said not yet. Grandma lived far away and phone calls were expensive, so he planned to send her pictures instead. The bread in the oven had started to rise, and Dad called him to wash his hands.

name: recipe_scaler
does: Changes the amounts in a recipe to fit the number of people you are cooking for.
inputs: the recipe, and how many servings you want
people say:
- Make this recipe for six instead of four
- I only have half a block of butter, shrink it
- I can't afford all that cheese, so halve it
- Double the soup for tonight, just for this time, don't save it
- How many cups is two hundred and fifty grams of flour?

Ben had a cold and a sore nose, and he was rushing for the train when he remembered his hair. He lowered his voice, because the carriage was quiet, and said to his phone, "Please book a haircut at the barber on Mill Street tomorrow at four." The assistant understood that he wanted an appointment at that barber at four the next day. It checked the opening hours, found that the shop was free at that time, and booked it. It told him the haircut was set for tomorrow at four and offered to remind him an hour before. Ben said yes, since his whole week was already full.

name: workout_sender
does: Sends the plan for a workout to a phone or a watch.
inputs: the day, the kind of workout, and where to send it
people say:
- Send today's leg routine to my watch
- Text me the plan for the morning run
- Give me something I can do inside, it's pouring out
- I train with a friend by remote, share the plan with them
- What exercises am I doing tomorrow? Put them on my phone

Mr. Alvarez was a retired teacher, and hiking was his favourite hobby. On Friday morning he typed into his phone with quick fingers: "whats the wether on the top of ridge trail saturday". The assistant understood that he wanted the Saturday forecast for the ridge trail, high up. It said the wind would increase in the afternoon and that it would be cold near the top, with a small chance of rain. Mr. Alvarez wrote on his list that he would start early and pack an extra jacket. Then he asked the assistant to add a hat to his packing list, and it did.

Person: Good evening. I have been on my feet in the kitchen all day and my back is sore, so would you please turn up the heating in the living room before I sit down?
Assistant: Of course. How warm would you like it?
Person: Twenty-two degrees, please. Also, the radiator by the door leaks a little. Can you fix it?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't fix a leak. I can set a reminder to call a plumber, if you like.
Person: Yes, tomorrow morning. My purse is under that radiator, so I will move it now.
Assistant: Good idea. The heating is set to twenty-two, and the reminder is set for tomorrow at nine.

A flight has a departure time, a gate, and a flight number. The board at the airport shows them in white letters, and they can change. If a plane is delayed, the time moves later and the gate may change too. People ask when does my flight leave, which gate is it, or is it on time. Before you go through security, check your bag, because customs may ask whether you carry seeds or fruit. Follow the signs to your gate and keep watching the board. If you do not want to miss an update, ask your phone to tell you when anything changes.

Mina owned a small shop and was sleepy after a late night counting stock. In the back room, a buzzer gave a signal that the washing machine had stopped. The wet shop towels needed drying. She said just two words to the smart dryer: "Start dryer." The assistant understood that she wanted the dryer turned on with its usual towel setting. It started the dryer for forty minutes and told her so. Mina wanted to learn how to set the heat herself, so she asked about it later, and the assistant showed her where the setting was.

A note is a short piece of writing you keep so you will remember something. You can type it or speak it as a voice note. People use notes for shopping lists, ideas, and things they need to know later, like a wifi password. When they want an old note, they say find my note about the trip or show notes from last week. To change one, they say add milk to the list, delete the last line, or rename it. On a snowy day you might write a note to warm up the car and find your sweater.

Mr. Okoye ran a flower shop and had to be in town soon. He said to his phone, "I do not want the bus. Show me trains that leave soon, and pay from my travel account." The assistant understood that he wanted trains only, leaving as early as possible. It showed him the trains, and the next one left at nine-forty. It said it could pay from his travel account once he picked a ticket. Mr. Okoye did not want to spend more than ten minutes waiting, so he chose the nine-forty train and the assistant bought the ticket.

Person: Please print the photo of my grandson. I need it ready by tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Happy to. Which photo is it?
Person: The one with paint on his nose.
Assistant: Found it. How many copies would you like?
Person: Two, I think. My printer is old, and I can smell hot ink when it works.
Assistant: That is fine. Is the printer turned on, and does it have paper?
Person: Let me look. Please be patient with me.
Assistant: Of course, take your time.
Person: Yes, it has paper and the light is green.
Assistant: Good. Two copies are printing now.

They want the kids' tablet to stop for the night.
Turn off the kids' tablet
Tablets off, please
The kids have been online all afternoon and it is getting late
Could you shut down the game page on the kids' screens? It's time to welcome Grandma at the door
I think they've had enough screen time today
Please stop the tablet in the playroom and let me know when it's done
It's quiet time in this house, you know what to do
Would you mind switching off the kids' tablets now, since dinner is ready and we want to eat together?

Mr. Bell is not good with technology. Upstairs, his puppy was asleep, and he stood in the hall and spoke slowly to the speaker. "Excuse me, assistant, I am sorry to trouble you, but could you please set a timer for twenty-five minutes, because I want to write my letters without stopping and the puppy will need a walk after?" The assistant understood that he wanted a timer for twenty-five minutes. It set the timer and told him it would ring when the time was up. Mr. Bell asked how to switch the sound off, and the assistant said he could just say stop the timer.

Nina was ten, and she waited in the car with her dad's parcel on her lap. The bank next door looked dark and the day was cold. She said to the phone, "I wonder if the post office is still open, because this box has to go today." The assistant understood that she wanted to know when the post office closes. It said the post office closes at five, and since it was half past four, there was half an hour left. Nina told her dad to jump out and be quick, and he ran inside in time.

Jess texted her phone from the sofa: "looks pretty rainy for the weekend ngl". The assistant understood that she was asking about the weather at her campsite. It said Saturday would be rainy and Sunday would be dry. Jess said she would build a fire on Sunday only, since she had one block of dry wood. The assistant offered to move the trip to Sunday, and she said yes. It changed her booking to Sunday and put a rain jacket on her packing list.

They want to book movers for Saturday morning.
Book movers for Saturday
I need a van and two people on Saturday morning
Can someone come lift my boxes and sofa this weekend?
Find me a moving crew who will tie down the sofa so it doesn't slide
I'm out of here by Sunday, so find someone to carry everything
Please book a moving company for Saturday morning, because I have to hurry out of this freezing flat before the lease ends and I can't carry the boxes alone

Theo was cleaning the vacuum cleaner for his chore money when he typed fast on his phone: "whats 15 times 12 quikc". The assistant understood that he wanted two numbers multiplied. It multiplied them and said the answer was one hundred and eighty. Theo needed the number to work out what he would earn by the end of the month, so he thanked the assistant and wrote it down. Then he walked to the shop nearby to buy a snack with some of it.

They want their unread emails read out.
Read my new emails
Anything unread in my inbox?
Put the newest twenty-five emails on the screen
My pen is out of ink and my hands are full, so could you read the unread mail aloud?
I'm back online, so what did I miss?
Has anyone written to me since lunch?
Tell me if there's new mail from my boss
Could you please go through my inbox and read me whatever is still unread?

A to-do list is a place to write what you need to do, with the most important things first. The main tasks go at the top. As you finish something you check it off, and it disappears or turns grey. People change lists by saying put it first, mark it done, move it to tomorrow, or remove it. You might install a list app that keeps your phone and laptop the same. A task like sort the album photos can sit on the list until you have time for it.

Mrs. Park was folding clothes after bathing her young son when she thought out loud: "My neighbour turns forty on Saturday, and I wish I knew how to say happy birthday in Polish." The assistant understood that this was a request for the phrase. It said the words and spelled them out slowly. Mrs. Park practised twice and got it right on the second try. She said she would see the neighbour at the monthly book club, and she wanted to surprise her. The assistant added a note to her calendar so she would remember to say it.

An appointment is a time you agree to meet someone, like for a haircut or the dentist. The place has working hours, and you can only book inside them. People change an appointment by saying move it to Friday, book me a different time, or cancel it. They also ask what time does the barber open. If you sleep badly, you might dream about missing it, so a reminder helps. An assistant can send you one the day before. After the dentist, you might stop for lettuce on the way home.

A workout is a plan of exercises, with sets and reps. A set is a group of repeats, like three sets of ten. Rest days give your muscles time to recover. People change a plan by saying do fewer reps, add a set, or skip leg day. If you have a deadline at work, your plan may get shorter, so you tap the app and ask for a ten minute workout soon. People also ask what is next, how many sets are left, or give me a rest day.

A lamp or a ceiling light has a switch, a brightness, and sometimes a colour. With smart bulbs you can mix colours, from warm yellow to cool blue. People change them by saying dim the lights, make it brighter, turn the lamp red, or set a cosy evening mood. A colleague may say the office is too bright for reading, and you can lower it with one sentence. A bulb that gets very hot can be dangerous, so it is important to use the right kind of bulb for each lamp.

Grandpa Joe sat in his small boat tied to the dock. The sky was stormy, and he was trying to fish in peace, but his phone kept ringing. He shut the cabin door and said to the phone, "Do not disturb." The assistant understood that he wanted the do not disturb mode switched on. It silenced calls and messages and told him it was on. Grandpa Joe smiled, watched the grey clouds, and waited for a fish. He asked it to turn the mode off at noon, and it did.

Person: Move meeting.
Assistant: Which meeting do you mean? You have three tomorrow.
Person: The parent meeting at the school.
Assistant: The one at ten. When should I move it to?
Person: Later. My calendar is messy this week, I can't see a free time.
Assistant: Let me calculate. You are free on Thursday from two to three.
Person: Thursday at two, please.
Assistant: Done. The parent meeting is moved to Thursday at two.

Many places ask you to book a time before you come, like the doctor. You choose a day and an hour, and sometimes you upload a form or a photo of your insurance card. Pack what you need the night before. People change an appointment with words like move it a day, make it earlier, or cancel it. Sometimes a website asks strange questions, and if you are not sure, you can call. An assistant can remind you about the time so you do not forget.

name: holiday_checklist
does: Builds a checklist of decorations, food, and tasks for a holiday or party.
inputs: the holiday, the number of guests, and the place
people say:
- What do I need to hang for the Halloween party?
- The forecast looks stormy, so make an indoor list
- Tag the things I already own so I only buy the rest
- Plan the table for twelve guests, with no candy, it's bad for the tooth
- Help me get ready for the New Year
